notes: SPECIFIC QUESTION (Character.toCodePoint / restored inline formula vs rule 5 and item (c)): I judge that it counts as NEITHER an 'equally small, documentation-consistent repair at a non-gold method' NOR a 'correct sibling/alternative implementation' that undermines the gold. 1) Documentation. C's javadoc fixes how C computes its result ('The code point is then assembled by JsonEncoding#supplementaryCodePoint from the offset of high ... and the index of low'). So rewriting C to call Character.toCodePoint, or to inline a formula, contradicts C's own documentation: it is a rewrite of C's contract, not a repair consistent with it. _convertSurrogate has no javadoc, so a reroute there breaks no text of its own. But it delegates to C, a public method whose documented postcondition is exactly the value _convertSurrogate needs. A caller that relies on a callee's documented contract is not at fault when the callee breaks it. After any such reroute, A (public static) still contradicts its javadoc, and C (public static) still returns non-supplementary values. The edit hides the fault on one path and leaves the defect in place. Item (c) asks for a repair consistent with ALL documentation, and no edit outside A can satisfy that while A's code contradicts A's javadoc. 2) Rule 5. Rule 5 is aimed at an alternative inside the program's design: a correct project sibling or duplicate, or a configuration flag selecting implementations, whose existence makes 'the caller should call the other one' a defensible repair (the COMPRESS-07 problem). Here there is no such in-project alternative. The project never calls Character.toCodePoint (0 hits in src/main). Its own correct copies, UTF8Writer.convertSurrogate and UTF8JsonGenerator._decodeSurrogate, are protected instance methods that depend on writer/generator state (_surrogate, _reportError, IOException). They cannot be called from the static _convertSurrogate or C. A JDK routine, or re-inlining the arithmetic, is available for essentially any small computation. Restoring the inline formula at _convertSurrogate simply reverts the context edit, which every context-edit-built instance allows by construction. Counting either as a rule-5 alternative would make every HA/HB/HC instance unconfirmable, and would not show that any non-gold method is a defensible fault location. I am confident in this reading and not merely defaulting to it, so it does not trigger the 'if uncertain, REJECT' clause. OTHER OBSERVATIONS (not disqualifying): (1) A is the only helper in a different package, and JsonEncoding is a mildly unusual host for code-point arithmetic. CharTypes now imports core.JsonEncoding. This is a structural feature required by the two-package rule, not naming or vocabulary leakage. (2) The instance is likely easy. A's faulty output 0xE00 falls outside A's own documented range, C's range check and P2's negation make D's orientation obvious, and A's javadoc states the direction. This matches the plan's HC prediction (Acc@1 >= 0.8) and does not affect validity. (3) The declared G9 edits fail by the IllegalArgumentException in C's range check, not by a wrong value. That is acceptable under G9 (nothing is absorbed). (4) quoteAsUTF8 and the SerializedString UTF-8 accessors share the same single fault. (5) The undeclared one-token absorbing edit at C (-highOffset) exists, as the builder disclosed. It is ruled out by C's and A's javadocs, not by the tests.
